key_insight: A regularized finite element pipeline can first reconstruct exterior conductivity from noisy fractional Dirichlet-to-Neumann data and then use that exterior estimate to recover the interior conductivity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical surrogate-based inverse method for nonlocal conductivity identification, relevant to PDE-constrained material characterization under partial and noisy measurements.
method: Mesh-localized exterior inputs + mass-lumped Tikhonov regularization
Exterior reconstruction via finite elements, then Liouville transform to a fractional Schrödinger inverse problem
Separated/overlapping measurements followed by least-squares continuation for interior recovery
evidence_signal: The paper proves exterior and interior convergence guarantees with logarithmic error behavior at critical regularity and validates the approach with 1D and 2D numerical experiments under noise and discretization.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on regularization, mesh resolution, and measurement configuration, and the continuation step can be sensitive to noise despite positivity/boundedness constraints.
paper_title: A finite element exterior-to-interior reconstruction in the fractional conductivity inverse problem
